detailed_description: Image Adjustment applies the standard browser canvas filter chain to one uploaded image and lets you download the result as PNG. Pick an image file, then drag seven sliders: brightness 0-200%, contrast 0-200%, saturation 0-200%, hue rotate 0-360deg, blur 0-20px, grayscale 0-100%, and sepia 0-100%. The canvas redraws the original image with the combined ctx.filter string in real time. Reset returns all sliders to defaults, Download exports the current canvas as PNG. There are no per-channel RGB curves, unsharp masking, RAW or SVG support, WebGL/WebAssembly pipelines, histogram analysis, layer composites, or DPI/compression controls.
usage_steps: Click Upload Image and pick a raster image file
Drag the brightness, contrast, and saturation sliders between 0% and 200%
Drag the hue rotate slider between 0 and 360 degrees
Drag the blur slider between 0 and 20 pixels
Drag the grayscale and sepia sliders between 0% and 100%
Click Download to save the current canvas as a PNG, or Reset to restore default sliders
usage_examples: Lighten a slightly dark photo by pushing brightness and contrast
Turn a color image into a quick black-and-white version with the grayscale slider
Apply a soft vintage feel by mixing partial sepia with a gentle hue rotate
Add a subtle blur to a background image before downloading the PNG

faqs.question: What image adjustments are available?
faqs.answer: The tool provides brightness, contrast, saturation, hue rotation, blur, grayscale, and sepia controls using the browser canvas filter chain.

faqs.question: What format does the download use?
faqs.answer: The adjusted image is exported from the canvas as a PNG file.

faqs.question: Does it edit RAW files or SVG images?
faqs.answer: No. It is intended for common raster image files that the browser can draw to a canvas.

faqs.question: Can I reset the edits?
faqs.answer: Yes. The reset action restores the default slider values so you can start again from the uploaded image.

faqs.question: Are the adjustments destructive?
faqs.answer: The original file is not changed. The tool draws an adjusted preview and lets you download a new PNG copy.
